Karthik / Emma — I pulled the forecast and sketched a sizing plan (attached). Key assumptions below: average response ~= 320 tokens; 95th pctl tails ~900 tokens; 70% of traffic is interactive (low latency), 30% is async/batch.

Recommended baseline pool (APAC primary, EU overlay):
- APAC (Singapore) dedicated pool: 8 H100-equivalent slots for hot serving + 6 A100-equivalent for background batching and KV/cache warmers. This targets a steady-state capacity with headroom for 2x expected short spikes.
- EU (Ireland) overlay: 3 H100-equivalent slots for geo-routed interactive traffic, with cross-region bursting to APAC as fallback.
- Burst lanes: enable on-demand burst capacity of up to 6 H100-equivalent instances across regions for 2-hour windows; bill-as-you-go.
- Canary cadence: 2-week canary (start 2027-04-04) with traffic ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% across 10 days, with rollback triggers on token error rate or 99th pctl latency > baseline + 60ms.

Operational notes:
- We recommend KV prefix caching for warm conversations (saves ~15-25% tokens on repeat traffic).
- If Lumina wants hard latency SLOs, lock H100 for 80% of interactive capacity; otherwise a mixed H100/A100 profile reduces cost ~18%.

I attached a quick cost/runbook spreadsheet with tradeoffs (redwood_capacity_reco_apac_eu.xlsx). If you confirm the token profile and canary SLAs, I'll mark the nodes for hold and surface lead time to Procurement.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_reco_apac_eu.xlsx

Thanks,
